$A$ and $B$ are points on the circumference of a circle, centre $O.$ 
$CA$ and $CB$ are tangents to the circle.

![q13-paper6-june2017-ocr-gcse-maths](assets/001-q13-paper6-june2017-ocr-gcse-maths.png)

By showing that at least one angle and all three sides are equal, show that triangle $OAC$ is congruent to triangle$OBC.$
parts.solution_md:
> *Congruent means 'identical to'*

> *Triangles **AOC** and triangles **BOC** are both **right-angled triangles *

*Angle *$OAC=OBC=90^{\circ}$ 
*(angle between tangent and radius *$=90^{\circ}$*)*

**[1]**

> *The side **OC** is in both triangles*

**OC ***is a common side in both triangles*

> * **OA **and **OB **are both radiuses of the same circle*

* ***OA*** = ***OB**
*(they are both radiuses of the same circle)*

**[1]**

> *AC **and **BC **are tangents to a circle from the same point*

* ***AC*** = ***BC**
*(tangents to a circle from the same point are equal)*

**All reasons must be given clearly for full marks [1]**

![Diagram has a circle centre O and two tangents from a single point outside the circle (A) to points B and D on the circle. Angles marked are 40°, 70°, and 75°. Note states "Diagram NOT accurately drawn".](assets/002-diagram-has-a-circle-centre-o-and-two-tangents-f.png)

$B,C$ and $D$ are points on the circumference of a circle, centre $O$. 
$ABE$ and $ADF$ are tangents to the circle.

Angle $DAB=40^{\circ}$ 
Angle $CBE=75^{\circ}$
Angle $BCD=70^{\circ}$

i) Explain why **reflex **angle $BOD=220^{\circ}$.

[3]

ii) Work out the size of angle $ODC$.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Locate the angle requested by following the line from point *$B$* to point *$O$* to point *$D$* and choosing the angle that is greater than 180*<sup>*o*</sup>

![Diagram from question with reflex angle BOD marked x](assets/003-diagram-from-question-with-reflex-angle-bod-mark.png)

> *Find the angles **ABO** and angle **ADO*

*Angle ***ABO*** = Angle ***ADO*** = 90**<sup>o</sup>**   *
*(Angle between a tangent and a radius is 90**<sup>o</sup>**)*

**Either right angle marked [1]**

![Diagram from question with right angles added at ABO and ADO](assets/004-diagram-from-question-with-right-angles-added-at.png)

> *Find angle **BOD*

*Two tangents from a point are equal so ***AD = AB*** *

*Angle ***BOD*** + Angle ***BAD*** + Angle ***ADO*** + Angle ***ABO*** = 360**<sup>o</sup>**   (Angles in a quadrilateral = 360**<sup>o</sup>**)*

*Angle ***BOD*** + 40 + 90 + 90 = 360 *
*Angle ***BOD*** = 140**<sup>o</sup>*

** [1]**

![Diagram with angle BOD marked as 140](assets/005-diagram-with-angle-bod-marked-as-140.png)

> *Find the reflex angle **BOD*

*Reflex Angle ***BOD ***+ Obtuse Angle ***BOD*** = 360**<sup>o</sup>**   *
*(Angles around a point = 360**<sup>o</sup>**)*

**Reflex Angle ****BOD**** + 140 = 360 **
**Reflex Angle ****BOD**** = 220**<sup>**o**</sup>*<sup> </sup>***[1]**
**Clear working needed for marks to be gained**

ii) *Find angle **CBO*

*Angle ***CBO*** + Angle ***ABO*** + Angle ***CBE*** = 180**<sup>o</sup>**   *
*(Angles along a straight line = 180**<sup>o</sup>**)*

*Angle ***CBO*** + 90 **<sup>o</sup>**+ 75**<sup>o</sup>** = 180**<sup>o</sup>*
*Angle ***CBO*** = 15**<sup>o</sup>*

**[1]**

![Diagram from question with angle of 15 degrees added at CBO ](assets/006-diagram-from-question-with-angle-of-15-degrees-a.png)

> *Find angle **ODC*

*Angle ***ODC*** + Angle ***DCB*** + Angle ***CBO*** + Reflex Angle ***BOD***  = 360**<sup>o</sup>*
*(Angles in a quadrilateral = 360**<sup>o</sup>**)*

*Angle ***ODC ***+ 70 + 15 + 220 = 360*

**Angle ****ODC ****= 55**<sup>**o**</sup><sup> </sup>**[1]**

$A$ and $B$ are points on a circle.
$PA$ and $PB$ are tangents.

![q21a-paper-3h-nov-2020-aqa-gcse-maths](assets/007-q21a-paper-3h-nov-2020-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

i) Work out the size of angle $ABP$.
Give a clear reason for your answer.

[2]

ii) Work out the size of angle $APB$.
Give a clear reason for your answer.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Locate the angle requested by following the line from point *$A$* to point *$B$* to point *$P$

> *Two tangents from a circle to the same point outside of the circle are equal lengths*

> *This means that triangle *$ABP$* **is isosceles*

*Angle *$ABP=$* Angle *$BAP$*   *
*(Base angles in an isosceles triangle are equal)*

**Angle **$ABP=71^{\circ}$** ****[1]**
**Two tangents from a point to a circle are equal**** [1]**

ii) *Locate the angle requested by following the line from point *$A$* to point *$P$* to point *$B$

> *Find the angle *$APB$*using the sum of the angles in a triangle*

*Angle *$APB$* + Angle *$ABP$* + Angle *$BAP=180^{\circ}$*   *
*(Angles in a triangle = 180**<sup>o</sup>**)*

*Angle *$APB+71+71=180$

*Angle *$APB=180-2(71)$

**Angle **$APB=38^{\circ}$ **[1]**
**The angles in a triangle add up to **$180^{\circ}$ **[1]**
